title: A profinite cover with countably many dense double fibres
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. There exist nonempty metrizable profinite spaces $T,V$, where profinite means compact Hausdorff totally disconnected and metrizable means that the topology is induced by a metric, a continuous surjection $q:T\to V$, distinct points $(v_k)_{k\geq0}$ of $V$, and points $t_k^-,t_k^+\in T$ with the following properties. The fibre over $v_k$ is exactly $\{t_k^-,t_k^+\}$ with $t_k^-\ne t_k^+$; every fibre over $V\setminus\{v_k:k\geq0\}$ is a singleton. In the relation space
$$R=T\times_VT=\{(x,y)\in T^2:q(x)=q(y)\},$$
with the subspace topology, each singleton $\{(t_k^-,t_k^+)\}$ and $\{(t_k^+,t_k^-)\}$ is open and closed. Finally, for every nonempty open subset $U\subseteq T$ and every integer $N\geq0$, there is $k\geq N$ such that $t_k^-,t_k^+\in U$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cantor-two-sided-dense-enumeration] to $V=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$. Compose its bijection $\mathbb N\to D$ with $D\hookrightarrow V$ to obtain the distinct sequence $(v_k)$ with range $D$, and regard its coordinate $c:V\to[0,1]$ as real-valued by inclusion. Put $A=V\setminus D$. The lemma gives nonempty metrizable profinite $V$, dense $A$, two-sided approximation at every $v_k$, and density of every enumeration tail.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; assembly Step 1

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-summable-jump-graph-compactification] to these data: the real coordinate is continuous and injective, the enumeration has range $D$ and no repetitions, and the required density and side sequences come from Step 1. With $a_k=2^{-k-3}$, form its $f$, $g_k$ and graph closure $T$, and take the first projection $q$. It gives nonempty metrizable profinite $T$, continuous surjective $q$, exactly the two distinct fibre points $t_k^-,t_k^+$ over $v_k$, and singleton fibres elsewhere. Its dense graph $\Gamma$ consists of points with singleton whole fibres.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; assembly Step 2

proof.text: Let $H:T\to\mathbb R$ be the second coordinate of $T\subseteq V\times[-1/4,1/4]$; it is continuous by the product and subspace topologies. The explicit fibre points of [lem-sfb-summable-jump-graph-compactification] give $H(t_k^+)-H(t_k^-)=(g_k+a_k)-(g_k-a_k)=2a_k=2^{-k-2}>0$. That lemma also gives Hausdorff $T$ and singleton fibres outside $D$. Apply [lem-sfb-dyadic-height-relation-isolation] to this same $q,H,v,t^-,t^+$; its relation is exactly the subspace $T\times_VT$ in our statement, so both required ordered-pair singletons are clopen.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; assembly Step 3

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dense-singleton-fibres-tail-lifting] with $S=\Gamma$. Step 2 supplies compact Hausdorff $T$, Hausdorff $V$, and continuous surjective $q$. It also gives dense $\Gamma$ and, for every $s=(x,f(x))\in\Gamma$, the whole fibre $q^{-1}(\{q(s)\})=\{s\}$. Step 1 supplies tail density of $v$. Thus every nonempty open $U\subseteq T$ and $N$ admit $k\ge N$ with $q^{-1}(\{v_k\})\subseteq U$. Step 2 identifies this fibre as $\{t_k^-,t_k^+\}$, so both points lie in $U$. This verifies the last clause.

lean.statement: theorem exists_countable_split_profinite_cover : ∃ (T V : Profinite.{u}), Nonempty T ∧ Nonempty V ∧ TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace T ∧ TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace V ∧ ∃ (q : C(T, V)), Function.Surjective q ∧ ∃ (v : ℕ → V) (tMinus tPlus : ℕ → T), Function.Injective v ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, tMinus k ≠ tPlus k ∧ q ⁻¹' {v k} = {tMinus k, tPlus k}) ∧ (∀ y : V, y ∉ Set.range v → ∃! x : T, q x = y) ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, IsClopen {r : {p : T × T // q p.1 = q p.2} | r.val = (tMinus k, tPlus k)} ∧ IsClopen {r : {p : T × T // q p.1 = q p.2} | r.val = (tPlus k, tMinus k)}) ∧ (∀ U : Set T, IsOpen U → U.Nonempty → ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ tMinus k ∈ U ∧ tPlus k ∈ U)
